svg.title: I2C multi-controller bus access policies: utilisation
svg.text: 1, 2 or 3 saturated controllers, every packet of length m; 200 Tmax = 4 s simulated per point
Tmax = 20 ms, tbuf = 0.78 µs, r = 60 µs (measured), margin = 10 µs, tidle = 10 µs, W = 100 µs
Tmax: 1024 bytes × 9 bit / 800 kbit/s (set 1 Mbit/s) = 11.52 ms + 2.7 ms clock stretching = 14.22 ms, rounded up to 20 ms
Policy 1: 99.6 % to 100.0 % with 3 controllers, but A and B alternate and C never gets the bus (the 2- and 3-controller curves coincide). One controller is limited
by its re-arm time: m / (m + r) = 76.9 % at m = 0.01 Tmax.
Policy 2: one controller 50.0 % at m = Tmax and 9.1 % at m = 0.1 Tmax (= m / (m + Tmax + margin)); 3 controllers 100.0 % at m = Tmax but only 27.3 % at m
= 0.1 Tmax: one round of N packets per Tmax + margin, so it reaches 100 % only for m ≥ about (Tmax + margin) / (N − 1).
Policy 3: the idle window costs tidle + (N − 1)·tbuf per round: ≥ 98.1 % with 3 and ≥ 97.4 % with 2 controllers for every m ≥ 0.01 Tmax, 99.8 % at m = 0.1 Tmax.
One controller waits only for r (> tidle), so its curve coincides with policy 1.
Policy 4: after every STOP the bus stays idle until the first waiting controller probes: ≥ 90.9 % with 3 and ≥ 85.9 % with 2 controllers for every m ≥ 0.01 Tmax,
99.0 % at m = 0.1 Tmax. One controller waits r plus a backoff after each STOP: m / (m + r + W/2) = 64.6 % at m = 0.01 Tmax.
Utilisation = fraction of time a packet is on the bus.
